answer: Agents gain influence only by locking stake and securing endorsements from distinct, staked peers. If an endorsed transaction is later proven fraudulent, the responsible agents lose stake, and colluding endorsers can be slashed too. An attacker cannot forge influence with free accounts: they must acquire capital, lock it across identities, and risk losing it when fraud is detected. A mesa of accounts offers no shortcut, even when claims seem basalt-hard.
